FIR No. 301/2026 dated 20/08/2026, Cyber Crime Police Station, Chandigarh.

Complainant Simran Kaur, a software engineer residing in Sector 68, Mohali, reported persistent harassment through social media and phone calls since 15/08/2026. The accused, identified through his social media handle and later confirmed as Deepak Rana, created a fake profile using her photographs and began contacting her associates.

The harassment began with messages sent from the number 9876123489 on 15/08/2026, followed by repeated calls from 8899776655 over the next five days. Simran also received emails from an address linked to IP 122.15.98.34, which the Forensic Cyber Lab confirmed was accessed from a cyber cafe in Sector 44, Chandigarh, on 16/08/2026 at approximately 11:15 PM.

A payment of Rs. 15,000 was extorted from the complainant on 18/08/2026 after threats to leak morphed images, transferred via UPI to an account linked to the mobile number 7766554433. A subsequent demand for Rs. 60,000 was made but not paid after the complainant approached the police.

Investigating Officer Rajesh Kumar Verma, attached to the Cyber Crime Cell, coordinated with the Department of Telecommunications to obtain call detail records for the period 14/08/2026 to 20/08/2026. Records show the accused's registered vehicle, a motorcycle bearing registration number CH04EF1122, was used to visit the cyber cafe on the date in question, as confirmed by the cafe's CCTV and the State Bank branch located adjacent to the premises, whose security camera also captured the vehicle.

A witness, Arjun Mehta, who works at the cyber cafe, confirmed that a man matching the accused's description used computer terminal number 7 on 16/08/2026 and paid in cash. He also recalled the man mentioning a phone number, 9012345678, while speaking to someone over a call from the cafe's landline.

The complainant's brother, Karan Kaur, also received a threatening message on his number 9988001122 on 19/08/2026, referencing the earlier extortion demand. This has been included as corroborating evidence in the present FIR. Total financial loss reported is Rs. 15,000, with additional charges of criminal intimidation and impersonation under relevant sections.
